title: 限时写作：流程、地图与阶段测评 · Four listening sections
instructions: 原创模拟训练材料；先独立作答，再核对依据。四节音频共40题，按顺序听音作答。合成训练音频时长不同于正式考试。
transcript:
Section 1: Planning a Community Art Project

Mia: Hi, Tom! Are you still working on the community art project for the library?
Tom: Yes, I am. But I'm a bit worried. The deadline is next Friday, and we still have a lot to do. There's a lot riding on this, so I want to make sure everything goes smoothly.
Mia: What's the plan? Maybe I can help.
Tom: Thanks! First, the design needs to be finished by Wednesday. Then the materials must be ordered. After that, we can start painting on Thursday.
Mia: So the design comes before ordering materials?
Tom: Exactly. And the painting must be done in the main hall, not outside, because of the weather. We can't risk the paint getting ruined by rain.
Mia: I see. Where will the painting be displayed?
Tom: It will be shown in the library's entrance area. The wall there is big and bright, so it should catch everyone's attention as soon as they walk in.
Mia: That sounds great. How many people are working on it?
Tom: At the moment, five of us. But we need at least eight to finish on time. We're a bit short-handed.
Mia: I can ask my sister and her friend. They are both good at painting.
Tom: That would be a big help! Also, we need to buy more paint. We've already used half of it.
Mia: How much paint do we need?
Tom: We need ten more bottles of blue paint and five of green.
Mia: OK. I'll go to the art shop tomorrow. Oh, wait—I heard the shop is closed on Mondays.
Tom: Really? Then we should go on Tuesday instead. Good catch!
Mia: No problem. By the way, has the library approved the design?
Tom: Not yet. They will review it on Monday morning. If they don't like it, we'll have to change some parts. So we're keeping our fingers crossed.
Mia: I hope they like it. The design looks amazing.
Tom: Thanks. I'm also thinking of adding some small stars around the edges. What do you think?
Mia: I think that's a nice idea. It will make it more lively.
Tom: Great. So, to sum up: design by Wednesday, order materials, paint on Thursday, and display in the entrance area. And we need more people and paint.
Mia: Right. I'll help with the paint and ask my sister. Let's meet again on Tuesday to check everything.
Tom: Perfect. See you then!

Section 2: City Library Writing Workshop: Changes and Directions

Good morning, everyone. Welcome to the City Library. My name is Sarah, and I’m the workshop coordinator. Today I’ll give you some practical information about our new writing workshop, which starts next week. I’m glad to see so many of you here, and I hope this short talk will answer most of your questions before the workshop begins.

First, let me explain the schedule. The workshop will be held every Tuesday evening from 6:30 to 8:30, starting on the 5th of March. It will run for eight weeks. Please note that the library closes at 9:00, so we must finish on time. The workshop is free, but you need to register online. Registration opens on the 20th of February, so please mark that date in your diary and register early, because places are limited.

Now, about the location. The workshop will take place in the Green Room, which is on the second floor. When you come in through the main entrance, walk past the information desk and take the stairs or the lift to the second floor. The Green Room is at the end of the corridor, next to the art gallery. There will be signs to help you, so you should not get lost.

Let me tell you about the workshop content. Each session will focus on a different writing skill. The first session is about planning your writing. The second session covers writing clear sentences. In the third session, we will practice writing short paragraphs. The fourth session is about linking ideas. The fifth session focuses on describing places. The sixth session is about describing changes. The seventh session is a review, and the eighth session is a final assessment. You will receive feedback on your writing from the tutor, which will help you improve step by step.

There are a few rules. Please bring your own notebook and pen. Laptops are allowed, but please turn off your phone during the workshop. Also, if you miss more than two sessions, you may not receive a certificate at the end.

Finally, I’d like to mention some changes to the library facilities. The café on the ground floor is currently closed for renovation. It will reopen on the 10th of March. The computer room has been moved to the first floor, and the quiet study area is now on the third floor. The main reading room is unchanged.

If you have any questions, please ask me after this talk, or send an email to the library. Thank you for listening.

Section 3: Planning a Timed Writing Task: Process, Map, and Progress Check

Tutor: Good morning, everyone. Today we’re going to discuss your timed writing task on processes and maps. Let’s start with the process diagram. Maria, can you explain the first stage?
Maria: Yes. The process begins with collecting used paper. Then it is sorted by hand. After that, it is washed and dried.
Tutor: Good. And what happens next?
Maria: The dried paper is then mixed with water to make pulp. The pulp is spread onto a screen and pressed to remove water. Finally, it is dried again and rolled into sheets.
Tutor: Excellent. Now, let’s look at the map. This map shows a town center before and after redevelopment. What are the main changes?
James: In the past, there was a factory near the river. Now it has been replaced by a park. Also, the small shops on the main street have been converted into a shopping mall.
Tutor: Correct. And what about the road?
James: The road that used to go through the center has been moved to the north. A new bridge has been built across the river.
Tutor: Good. Now, let’s talk about the structure of your essay. How should you organize the process description?
Maria: We should use sequencing words like ‘first’, ‘then’, ‘after that’, and ‘finally’. And we should use the passive voice because the focus is on the process, not the person.
Tutor: Exactly. And for the map, what tense should you use?
James: For the past, we use the past simple passive, like ‘was built’. For the present, we use the present perfect passive, like ‘has been built’.
Tutor: Right. Now, let’s discuss the progress check. You will have a timed writing task next week. You will have 20 minutes to write about 150 words. Remember to check your work for passive voice and linking words.
Maria: Will we be allowed to use a dictionary?
Tutor: No, dictionaries are not allowed. But you can use a plan. Now, any questions?
James: How will the task be marked?
Tutor: The task will be marked for task achievement, coherence, vocabulary, and grammar. You will receive a score for each. Now, let’s review the stages of the process again. Maria, can you list them in order?
Maria: First, collection. Second, sorting. Third, washing and drying. Fourth, mixing with water. Fifth, spreading and pressing. Sixth, final drying and rolling.
Tutor: Perfect. Now, let’s talk about the map. James, what was the factory replaced by?
James: It was replaced by a park.
Tutor: And what happened to the small shops?
James: They were converted into a shopping mall.
Tutor: Good. Now, remember to use the passive voice and sequencing words. Also, make sure your map description is clear and well-organized. That’s all for today.

Section 4: The Community Garden Project: From Plan to Harvest

Good morning, everyone. Today I want to talk about a community garden project that was started in our town last year. I'd like to explain how the project began, how the land was prepared, and what has happened since. I hope this talk will be useful for anyone thinking about starting a similar project in their own area, and I will try to describe each stage clearly so that you can follow the whole process from the first idea to the present day.

The project was designed by a local group called Green Spaces, and it was supported by the town council. The aim was to turn an unused piece of land into a garden where people could grow vegetables and flowers. The land was chosen because it was close to the town centre and had good sunlight. However, the soil was not very good, so it had to be improved before planting could begin. This early stage took more time and effort than the group had expected, but it was seen as an essential step for the success of the whole garden.

First, the ground was cleared of rubbish and stones. Then, compost was added to make the soil richer. This work was done by volunteers over several weekends. After that, the garden was divided into small plots, and each plot was given to a family or an individual. The plots were arranged in rows, with a path running between them. A shed was built at the back of the garden to store tools, and a water tank was installed near the entrance. These simple facilities made it much easier for people to work in the garden regularly.

The garden was officially opened in April, and since then it has been used by many people. The number of volunteers has increased from ten to thirty. The garden has also become a place for social events, such as picnics and workshops. One workshop on growing tomatoes was very popular. The project has been so successful that similar gardens are now being planned in other parts of the town. The council has promised to provide more land if the community wants to expand.

In the future, the garden will be extended to include a small orchard. Fruit trees will be planted along the northern edge. The project shows how a neglected space can be transformed into a valuable community resource. Thank you for listening.

grammar.title: 被动语态、顺序、地点、变化及句子间衔接
grammar.explanation: 本对话中使用了被动语态（如 'the design needs to be finished'）、顺序词（first, then, after that）、地点表达（in the main hall, in the entrance area）以及变化表达（make it more lively）。句子间使用连接词如 'but', 'and', 'so' 来衔接。
grammar.example: First, the design needs to be finished by Wednesday. Then the materials must be ordered. After that, we can start painting on Thursday.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct passive form: The painting ______ in the main hall.
questions.explanation: 被动语态表示‘画必须被完成’，结构为 must be + 过去分词。
questions.evidence: the painting must be done in the main hall

questions.prompt: Which word correctly completes the sequence? First, finish the design. ______, order the materials.
questions.explanation: 顺序词 Then 表示‘然后’，用于描述步骤。
questions.evidence: Then the materials must be ordered.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct preposition: The painting will be displayed ______ the entrance area.
questions.explanation: 表示在某个空间内部用介词 in。
questions.evidence: It will be shown in the library's entrance area.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly links two ideas with a contrast?
options: The design is good, but it needs some changes.
The design is good, so it needs some changes.
The design is good, because it needs some changes.
The design is good, and it needs some changes.
answers: The design is good, but it needs some changes.
questions.explanation: but 表示转折，符合‘设计好但需要修改’的逻辑。
questions.evidence: If they don't like it, we'll have to change some parts.
